cf.title: Add a permission check to pg_stat_get_backend_subxact()

input.subject: Add a permission check to pg_stat_get_backend_subxact()

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only one raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because v12 keeps a comment on pgstat_fetch_stat_backend_by_pid() about data from an older backend. The patch applies the existing HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS() rule to four functions, on HEAD only, after pgsql-security asked for a consistency fix and a committer agreed in message #3. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 27 messages and no code were read.

brief.title: Permission checks for four per-backend statistics functions
brief.problem: pg_stat_get_backend_subxact(), pg_stat_get_backend_io(), pg_stat_get_backend_wal() and pg_stat_get_backend_lock() return a session's details to any caller, unlike their sibling functions that call HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS(). The author reported it to pgsql-security, which judged it not a vulnerability and asked for a consistency fix on HEAD.
brief.proposed_design: The four functions call HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS() and hide their output from callers who are not superuser, do not have pg_read_all_stats, and are not members of the owning role. PgStat_Backend stores the owning role OID at entry creation, and the io, wal and lock functions check against it, because a stats snapshot may hold data of an older backend with the same proc number.
user_visible_surface: pg_stat_get_backend_subxact() returns NULL to callers without statistics privileges.
pg_stat_get_backend_io() and pg_stat_get_backend_lock() return no rows to such callers.
pg_stat_get_backend_wal() returns NULL to such callers.
Stats of processes owned by no role, such as autovacuum workers and the WAL writer, become visible only to superusers and pg_read_all_stats.
PgStat_Backend gains a role OID field, which changes the struct layout seen by C code.
author_claims: The change makes these functions consistent with the other per-backend functions and with pg_stat_activity.
pid, dbid, userid and idset leak nothing new, since pg_stat_get_activity() already shows them to every caller.
Checking the role stored in the stats entry closes the snapshot case where an unprivileged role read a superuser session's IO and WAL numbers.
The change alters output for unprivileged callers, so it is for HEAD only, with no backpatch.
brief.thread_state: Michael Paquier committed the doc fix for subxact_overflowed, and the PID-in-entry and ProcNumberGetTransactionIds() patches were dropped at his request. solai v tested v12 and found no issues, and no committer has said v12 is ready.
unclear: The material does not say whether monitoring tools that call these functions as unprivileged roles break, or how many exist.
Bertrand's race in pgstat_read_current_status() between the userid and the subxact counters stays unfixed after v11-0002 was dropped.
The material does not say how stats entries created before upgrade or after a stats reset get a valid role OID, beyond the reset callback note.
The thread does not say whether a follow-up handles cross-stats-kind snapshot reuse, as with replication slot stats.

prior_attempts.title: Restrict EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) for RLS and security_barrier views
prior_attempts.quote: Therefore, restricting EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) will do more harm than good, since it will make analyzing query performance harder without a real security gain.
prior_attempts.reason: Dean Rasheed noted that the issue is not a security bug and that row counts can also be seen through pg_stat_get_tuples_returned(), pg_class.reltuples and plain EXPLAIN estimates, so EXPLAIN should stay as it is. After a discussion on pgsql-security, the author marked the patch rejected. The reason was that a determined attacker who can run arbitrary SQL can subvert row-level security anyway, so the restriction makes performance analysis harder without a real security gain.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P9 blocked a whole command for every unprivileged user. This patch applies the existing HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS() rule, so session owners and pg_read_all_stats members still see the numbers, as in pg_stat_activity.

refuted.title: Two sources of the owning role for one family of functions
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a pg_stat_get_backend_* function for a new cumulative stats field and copies the beentry-based check from pg_stat_get_backend_subxact(). Under stats_fetch_consistency = snapshot, that function shows a superuser session's numbers to an unprivileged role. No test or assertion catches it, so the leak surfaces only in a field report.
refuted.argument: v12 checks pg_stat_get_backend_subxact() against the beentry role, but checks io, wal and lock against the role stored in PgStat_Backend (message #17, commit message). Message #13 showed that the beentry check is unsafe for snapshot data, and the reviewers found this only on the third pass (messages #8, #13). The per-backend table now has two correct patterns. Choosing between them depends on where the data comes from, and nothing enforces that choice. The proposal adds no comment or helper that names the rule for future functions.
refuted.author_must_show: Where does v12 state, in code or a helper, which role a future per-backend function must check, so that copying the subxact pattern fails loudly?

critic.reasoning: Message #23 says v11-0001, kept as v12, adds a comment to pgstat_fetch_stat_backend_by_pid() that cached statistics may belong to an older backend. A future cumulative function calls that fetch function, and the commit message states that the check uses the role stored with the data.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: PgStat_Backend gains a role OID field; whether the stats file format needs a version bump can only be checked in the code.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The new role OID field changes the layout of PgStat_Backend in pgstat.h, which C extensions can see.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Four functions start to hide session details from callers without pg_read_all_stats, superuser, or membership in the owning role.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The output change for unprivileged callers is HEAD only; only the subxact_overflowed doc fix was backpatched.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The subxact function checks the backend status entry role, while io, wal and lock check the role stored in PgStat_Backend.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which role OID does a PgStat_Backend entry hold after a stats reset, and for an entry read from a stats file written before the upgrade?
Do known monitoring tools call these four functions as a role without pg_read_all_stats, and does the change need a release note entry for them?
Is the race in pgstat_read_current_status() between the userid and the subxact counters accepted as existing behaviour, or is a follow-up planned?
Is a follow-up planned for snapshot reuse across other stats kinds, such as replication slot stats?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier takes part in the thread, committed the doc fix and steered the design; the owner needs to know the cumulative statistics and backend status code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a visibility change in four monitoring functions and for a new role OID field in PgStat_Backend that future per-backend functions must check correctly. The change is small and limited to HEAD.
committability.author_follow_up: The author revised the patch through v12 in about two months and dropped two patches at the committer's request, which suggests continued engagement.

priority.reason: The patch is about 16 KiB, touches only the statistics code, docs and one regression test, and copies an existing rule. A committer who knows the area is engaged and a reviewer tested v12 without findings.

provisional_note: Without the code, the handling of the stored role OID across stats reset, stats file reload and proc number reuse could not be checked. Whether the stats file format needs a version bump is also open.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add tracking of backend memory allocated to pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a column to pg_stat_activity that shows the bytes of memory currently allocated by each backend, updated as memory contexts malloc and free memory. Dynamic shared memory counts only for the backend that created it, and the value cannot go below zero.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the entry to merge it into the thread "Add the ability to limit the amount of memory that can be allocated to backends", where it continued as patch 0001. Justin Pryzby suggested closing this entry once the patches moved there. The thread did not reject the design. Earlier comments about widening pg_stat_activity and about accuracy were still open when the entry closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Per conversation in thread listed below, patches have been submitted to the "Add the ability to limit the amount of memory that can be allocated to backends" thread

precedents_retrieved.title: Get rid of pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the pgstat_count_backend_io_op*() functions, so I/O counters are incremented once, and copies the pending I/O stats into the per-backend pending stats when the I/O stats flush. To make this work, per-backend stats must flush after the other stats kinds, first by placing PGSTAT_KIND_BACKEND last in the enum and later (v3) by flushing it outside the loop in pgstat_report_stat().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the ordering dependency between stats kinds at flush time, which so far have been independent, and said the copy approach hurts readability. He also said there was no benchmark data to choose among inlining, static structures, copies or fewer diffs, so the picture was incomplete. Andres Freund rejected the alternative WalUsage-style diff approach as too costly. The thread ends with the author disagreeing, and the visible messages do not show a final decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Hmm.  I really have an issue with the ordering dependency this
introduces between stats kinds, assumed to happen inside the code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Invalid permission check in pg_stats for functional indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the pg_stats view so that statistics on expression index columns are visible to a user who has select privilege on all table columns the index expression uses. It finds those columns through pg_depend in a second privilege-check path in the view definition.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found the approach wrong for indexes that depend on whole-row variables, because it ignores pg_depend entries with refobjsubid = 0. He also noted that it breaks pg_stats for materialized views and foreign tables, and Alvaro Herrera reported a large performance drop. Tom proposed changing has_column_privilege() for indexes instead and posted a draft patch, but the author did not return and no one finished the work, so the entry was closed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's also flat out wrong for indexes that depend on whole-row
variables.  For that case, we really need to insist that the user
have select privilege on all the table columns, but this won't
accomplish that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add checkpoint stats of snapshot and mapping files of pg_logical dir
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds statistics about logical decoding snapshot and rewrite mapping files in pg_logical to the checkpoint complete log message, such as count, time and cutoff LSN. After review it was cut down to one aggregate time, "logical decoding processing", plus a separate patch that deduplicates the checkpoint/restartpoint log messages.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Earlier objections about message length and translation were addressed. Nathan Bossart marked v12 ready for committer, and the author set it back to ready for committer after an unrelated pg_upgrade test failure on Windows. The entry was then withdrawn with no visible explanation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adjust pg_stat_get_lock() prorows to match lock types
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes prorows for pg_stat_get_lock() in pg_proc.dat from 10 to 12, so the planner estimate matches the one row per lock type the function returns. It also adjusts two function comments in pgstat_lock.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said prorows is a rough planner estimate and does not need to match the exact row count, so a gap between 10 and 12 is not worth fixing. Keeping prorows in step with the number of lock types would add maintenance work each time a lock type is added, and no planning problem was shown. Michael Paquier pointed out that pg_stat_get_io() has prorows 30 but returns 95 rows.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Given that, I don't think a difference between 10 and 12 rows is worth
fixing. Keeping prorows synchronized with the exact number of lock
types would only add maintenance overhead whenever a new lock type is
introduced.

precedents_retrieved.title: Eliminating "Permission denied" errors on stat() (on Windows)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the Windows stat() replacement (_pgstat64) retry on ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, as pgwin32_open() already does, so that files in the "delete pending" state do not cause "could not stat file ... Permission denied" errors in functions such as pg_ls_waldir(). It also undoes the _NtQueryInformationFile() handling added in bed90759f and makes pgwin32_open() call the native stat().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier committed the patch but reverted it the same day because it broke the MinGW buildfarm member fairywren. The author sent a MinGW-compatible version, but Michael said he needed MinGW test infrastructure before looking at it again. The author then withdrew the entry in favor of Thomas Munro's "Check for STATUS_DELETE_PENDING on Windows" patch, which detects the status directly.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think that my patch should be withdrawn in favor of
https://commitfest.postgresql.org/34/3326/ ("Check for
STATUS_DELETE_PENDING on Windows" by Thomas Munro), that use deeper
understanding of the problematic status, not indirect indication of it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Improve management of SLRU statistics collection.
Reverted commit(s): Move each SLRU's lwlocks to a separate tranche.; Collect statistics about SLRU caches
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Instead of re-identifying which statistics bucket to use for a given
SLRU on every counter increment, do it once during shmem initialization.
This saves a fair number of cycles, and there's no real cost because
we could not have a bucket assignment that varies over time or across
backends anyway.

Also, get rid of the ill-considered decision to let pgstat.c pry
directly into SLRU's shared state; it's cleaner just to have slru.c
pass the stats bucket number.

In consequence of these changes, there's no longer any need to store
an SLRU's LWLock tranche info in shared memory, so get rid of that,
making this a net reduction in shmem consumption.  (That partly
reverts fe702a7b3.)

This is basically code review for 28cac71bd, so I also cleaned up
some comments, removed a dangling extern declaration, fixed some
things that should be static and/or const, etc.

precedents_retrieved.title: Restrict EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) for RLS and security_barrier views
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch forbids EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) for statements that use row-level security or security_barrier views, so ordinary users cannot see how many rows the policy or view condition filtered out. Only members of a predefined role, proposed as pg_read_all_stats, could still run it in those cases.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Dean Rasheed noted that the issue is not a security bug and that row counts can also be seen through pg_stat_get_tuples_returned(), pg_class.reltuples and plain EXPLAIN estimates, so EXPLAIN should stay as it is. After a discussion on pgsql-security, the author marked the patch rejected. The reason was that a determined attacker who can run arbitrary SQL can subvert row-level security anyway, so the restriction makes performance analysis harder without a real security gain.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Therefore, restricting EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) will do more harm than good, since it will make analyzing query performance harder without a real security gain.

precedents_retrieved.title: Check consistency of GUC defaults between .sample.conf and pg_settings.boot_val
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends the TAP test 003_check_guc.pl, with an SQL version too, so it checks that each default in postgresql.conf.sample matches pg_settings.boot_val. GUCs whose defaults depend on the platform or are set by initdb are excluded through new GUC flags (DEFAULTS_COMPILE, DEFAULTS_INITDB) and a hardcoded list of parameters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier did not want the test to depend on a hardcoded list of GUCs, because the existing test needs no such maintenance. At closing he also objected to the new backend GUC flags and to the extra logic needed for initdb-set and platform-dependent defaults, and preferred to keep 003_check_guc.pl checking parameter names only. The thread had no activity for more than 8 months, and vignesh C closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: FWIW, I am not really a fan of making this test depend on a hardcoded list of GUCs.

roaster_notes.note: The only listed precedent is a restriction with no real security gain, and this patch has that shape too, since pgsql-security judged it not a vulnerability. But it removes an exception to an existing rule, keeps access for owners and pg_read_all_stats, and a committer asked for it in message #3. The thread does not mention any earlier attempt at the same idea.

From the standards and compatibility angle the change follows existing practice: the four functions adopt the HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS() rule and the NULL or no-rows convention that their sibling functions and pg_stat_activity already use, it adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump state, and it is limited to HEAD. Unprivileged monitoring roles that read per-backend IO, WAL or lock numbers of other sessions will now get empty results without an error. That needs a release note entry, but it is the same behaviour pg_stat_activity already has. [P9] is about restricting EXPLAIN without a security gain, and the consistency argument for this patch was accepted in messages #3 and #8.

The only persistent change is a role OID field in PgStat_Backend, on HEAD only, with no WAL, catalog, protocol or pg_upgrade effect. Per-backend stats entries are dropped at backend exit, the reset callback keeps the field, and whether a stats file format bump is needed can only be checked in the code.

The patch tightens access, follows the existing HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS() rule used by pg_stat_activity and the sibling functions, and checks against the role stored in PgStat_Backend, which closes the snapshot case from message #13. [P9] does not apply because per-backend IO, WAL, lock and subxact numbers are not available elsewhere, and the subxact race was dropped in message #25 as existing pg_stat_activity behaviour.

Otherwise the change is small and copies existing practice. Michael Paquier is engaged and steered the design, and the costs fall only on callers of these functions. Nothing touches a hot path or adds a dependency.

No existing feature gives the same result. Revoking EXECUTE from PUBLIC would also hide a role's own sessions, while HAS_PGSTAT_PERMISSIONS() is the existing check the sibling functions already use, so the patch extends that check and adds no second mechanism.

This proposal tightens access on four existing functions to match their sibling functions and pg_stat_activity. It adds no feature, so the demand angle does not apply. pgsql-security asked for the consistency fix (message #1), and Michael Paquier and Bertrand Drouvot support it (messages #3, #8). Monitoring roles keep access through pg_read_all_stats. [P9] declined a restriction on EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) that brought no real security gain, but it does not fit here. That restriction removed a capability from all users, while this one only aligns four functions with an access rule that already covers the same data.
